Done. Both open findings on trail 1087 are addressed and resolved.

**What the findings said:** Both flagged the same defect in `cmd/entire/cli/textutil/ide_tags.go:22` — the `<timestamp>` regex matched anywhere in the prompt, so a user pasting XML or log text containing `<timestamp>2026-01-01</timestamp>` would have it silently deleted. Unlike the other stripped tags (`ide_*`, `local-command-*`), `timestamp` is ordinary XML vocabulary, so name alone can't distinguish Cursor's injection from user content.

**The fix (commit `979cbea67` on `fix/import-prompt-tags`):** Anchored the regex with `\A\s*`, so only a single-line `<timestamp>` block at the head of the message is stripped. That matches Cursor's actual injection shape — it prepends the send-time date before `<user_query>` (documented in `cursor/AGENT.md`). The trade is deliberate: a timestamp arriving anywhere else now leaks into a title at worst (cosmetic false negative), instead of ever corrupting user content.

Along the way:
- Updated the two test cases that had been pinning the old behavior — the pasted-XML case now asserts a leading timestamp is stripped while the embedded one survives, and the nested-`<timestamps>` case asserts full preservation.
- Noted the anchoring in the Cursor `AGENT.md` behavior list.
- Tests pass for `textutil`, `agentimport`, `agent/cursor`, and both `transcript` packages; fmt + lint clean.
- The remote branch had picked up a merge of `main` while I worked, so I rebased my single unpushed commit on top rather than force-pushing anything.
